behavior_followup.name: COMPUTE-RESTARTS
behavior_followup.arity: zero or one argument: optional condition (NIL means no condition filter)
behavior_followup.result_shape: ordered list of currently active restart objects; most recently established first; include anonymous and duplicate-name restart objects. A non-NIL condition retains restarts associated with it plus unassociated restarts.
behavior_followup.semantic_law: For an optional condition C, return the currently active restart objects in dynamic nesting order (innermost first). If C is non-NIL, exclude only restarts associated with a nonempty set of conditions that does not contain C. Preserve distinct restart objects even when their names are equal; preserve anonymous restarts whose RESTART-NAME is NIL. This is a read-only list observation: it does not invoke restarts.
positive_witnesses: Nested RESTART-BIND scopes: the inner restart precedes the outer restart in COMPUTE-RESTARTS output.

Two distinct restart objects with the same name and one anonymous restart are all present as distinct list members; WITH-CONDITION-RESTARTS filters an associated restart for a different condition while preserving unassociated restarts.
behavior_followup.falsifier: Any implementation that collapses same-name restart objects, drops the anonymous restart, reverses nested restart order, includes a restart associated only with another condition, or invokes a restart while merely listing it.

behavioral_dedup.D1-D9: Current foundation exact-name audit: no COMPUTE-RESTARTS name collision. Existing condition signaling and D2 control laws are not treated as a duplicate; the list-valued observation and ordering still require an explicit owner check.
behavioral_dedup.D10: Current 635-row inventory contains FIND-RESTART but not COMPUTE-RESTARTS. FIND-RESTART is a one-restart/name lookup and cannot produce the full ordered list with anonymous and same-name distinct entries. This witnesses a shape/observability distinction, not automatic Core authority.

behavior_followup.owner_gate: PENDING: the value law is distinct from FIND-RESTART lookup, but access to active restarts depends on D2 dynamic-control context. Owner must decide Core observation vs D2/library boundary.
behavior_followup.donor_revision: ANSI Common Lisp HyperSpec (X3.226-1994), §9.2 Dictionary entry 9.2.32; CLHS entry URL pinned above.

rows.name: COMPUTE-RESTARTS
rows.behavioral_dedup: A condition-filtered, ordered snapshot of all dynamically active restarts including anonymous and shadowed duplicate names; not equal to D8/D9 RESTART-BIND or RESTART-CASE (dynamic binding/control) or FIND-RESTART single-name lookup.
rows.owner_boundary: D10 observational read-only result, D2 retains restart binding, invocation and nonlocal control.
positive_witnesses: For nested same-name restarts and one anonymous restart, compute-restarts includes all three in innermost-first order; find-restart can return only the nearest same-name restart.
Given restarts associated with condition A and an unassociated restart, filtering by unrelated condition B removes A-specific restart but keeps unassociated restart.
falsifiers: Dropping an anonymous restart or a shadowed same-name restart violates the law.
Returning an unrelated-condition-specific restart for condition B or reversing nesting order violates the law.
rows.decision_reason: A list-valued observation is behaviorally distinct from FIND-RESTART's one-result lookup: output preserves active restart identity, nesting order, anonymous entries and duplicate names. It only observes the D2-established dynamic context and must not invoke/reorder any restart; final Core-vs-D2/library ownership remains pending.
